atlases.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Make one square raster asset atlas for an original first-grade math lesson set in a neighborhood community radio station. Four strictly equal quadrants, no separator or border, no elements cross between quadrants. Very fine paper texture, matte gouache, clean cut-paper contours, deep pine green and warm oat cream, apricot and persimmon accents, consistent polished picture-book aesthetic. No lettering, digits, signage, tiny decorative dots, emoji, logos, watermark, or intentional math diagrams in any quadrant. The exact quantities will be drawn by software later.
Top left quadrant: wide, cheerful cover composition showing two Chinese first-grade children setting up a small neighborhood radio studio, one young girl in amber and one young boy in forest green, a friendly rounded desktop microphone, pinboard and soft warm daylight. Put children on the right side, soft calm cream walls on the left.
Top right quadrant: clean game background of the studio's sorting workroom. The entire central 75 percent is an empty warm softly lit floor seen at a very shallow overhead angle, shelves and wall only at far top and outer edges. Low contrast, pine edges, good readability behind puzzle pieces.
Bottom left quadrant: clean game background facing the radio studio broadcast desk and its window, warm windowsill framing and pine trim at outer edges, central three-fourths and lower floor calm empty pale cream. No objects inside the central empty playing zone.
Bottom right quadrant: sprite tray on perfectly uniform solid pale mint background #d1ecda. Four small individual, widely separated objects in a precisely regular invisible 2-by-2 grid wholly inside this quadrant. Upper-left a side-view low radio station rolling trolley with warm orange handle pointing to the left and two wheels, upper-right a single amber rectangular scallop-edged blank radio entry ticket, lower-left a single green-lidded cream box of stage props, lower-right a single compact dark green microphone with small foot. Each object fully visible, occupies only the central 45% of its invisible subcell, no shadows or floor, no edge touching, no text, no marks indicating count. The rectangles of the quadrant must be plain mint from edge to edge.
